frontier.hypothesis: $a1 must be made to CONFLICT with `off`'s live range, not merely be un-preferred — preference removal is measured dead in both allocators.
frontier.mechanism: find_free_reg unions regs_live_at[ins] over [born_index, dead_index) into its `used` set (local-alloc.c:2168-2171), and global.c's find_reg does the analogous conflict-set exclusion. A form in which $a1 is LIVE strictly between `off`'s birth (the `idx << 5` shift) and its death (the `addu a1,...`) excludes $a1 for `off` in both passes, which is the only mechanism left that both allocators respect.
frontier.next_probe: Attack the SYMBOL pseudo (139), not `off`. Read the .loop movable log for regno 139 first (`pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80041BF4`) and find what would make move_movables decline to hoist `(set rN (symbol_ref D_800A9A24))` out of the loop body — this is a loop.c question of the same shape as the axis s2 closed one level out for D_80094DF0. If the symbol stays block-local it carries the same $a1 suggestion, and qty_sugg_compare ordering can give it $a1 first, forcing `off` to $v0 exactly as target has it. Confirm any candidate in ONE build with BB2_SUGG_DEBUG/BB2_QTY_DEBUG rather than sweeping spellings.
